A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the models and methods presented here are applicable to the analysis of data from capture-re-encounters of animals in the wild, and that the methods are particularly appropriate for the analysis of recovery data.

the use of the model described in this paper has been very useful in analysing the data sets that were available to us, and we hope that this work will stimulate the use of such models in the analysis of similar data.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the analysis of such data, one needs to incorporate covariates into the models.

the inclusion of covariates in capture re-encounters is important, especially when the covariates have a non-linear effect on the probability of re-encounters, and when the covariate is measured at the time of capture and is not known at the time of re-encounter.
, in order to avoid biased estimates of survival, the reporting/recapture probabilities must be modelled as functions of the covariates of interest.
